body.input: Which AI companies expanded to Denmark in 2026?

response.content:
Based on available information, here are notable AI-related company expansions into Denmark in 2026:

## Netcompany → Danish Centre for AI Innovation (DCAI)

The most prominent AI expansion in Denmark in 2026 is **Netcompany's** investment into the **Danish Centre for AI Innovation (DCAI)**, announced on **10 November 2026**. Netcompany acquired a **23.7% stake** in DCAI through a **DKK 325 million (~€47.7M)** investment, joining existing owners the **Novo Nordisk Foundation** and **EIFO** (Denmark's Export and Investment Fund). The total funding round was **DKK 500 million (~€67M)**. DCAI operates **Gefion**, Denmark's first AI supercomputer (an NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD with 1,528 NVIDIA H100 GPUs). The investment aims to expand Gefion into a scalable, secure, and commercially viable national AI platform for the Danish public sector, critical industries, and research institutions.

## Pax8 – Continued Focus on Denmark

**Pax8**, a cloud commerce marketplace company with AI and cybersecurity offerings, continued expanding its focus on the Danish market in 2026, building on its 2025 expansion to strengthen support for local managed service providers (MSPs).

## Rubrik – Hiring in Denmark

**Rubrik** (NYSE: RBRK), a cybersecurity and AI operations company, has been actively hiring in Denmark in 2026, including remote positions such as Account Executive roles, signaling an expansion of its commercial presence in the Danish market.

---

The Danish government's **2026 government platform** also set an ambition for Denmark to become a frontrunner in AI development and responsible application, with plans to provide DKK 150 million in additional public commitment through EIFO — creating a favorable environment for further AI company expansions.

# Danish Centre for AI Innovation raises DKK 500m and expands ownership with Danish IT firm Netcompany (publ.)

Press Release [...] Press Release

Netcompany will acquire a 23.7% stake in Danish Centre for AI Innovation (DCAI), the operator of Denmark’s AI supercomputer Gefion, through a DKK 325m investment. This comes as part of a DKK 500m funding round alongside existing investors EIFO and the Novo Nordisk Foundation, supporting further expansion of Gefion and newer Nvidia-based hardware to increase Denmark’s AI computing capacity for businesses, public institutions and researchers. The capital will facilitate faster investment in AI infrastructure, related technology and organisational build-out, while Netcompany will also contribute expertise in critical IT systems and AI governance. The round values DCAI at DKK 875m pre-money and DKK ~1,375m post-money.

Why Netcompany? The company plans to layer its Feniks Governance software and 24/7 operations onto Gefion's raw GPU capacity, turning it into an enterprise-grade platform. "Denmark will undoubtedly increase the use of responsible and sovereign AI — the question is whether the value is created here in Denmark or somewhere else," Rogaczewski said.

Why now? The deal lands as Europe steps up public-private investment in sovereign AI compute, with the EU's 2026 gigafactory initiative set to combine public funding with private capital. Netcompany says it will fund the stake through existing credit facilities and expects no change to its 2026 guidance. [...] The signal: The round reflects a broader push to keep AI infrastructure — and its economic upside — on national soil. By converting a GPU asset into a governed, commercial service, Netcompany and its co-investors are betting that sovereignty, not just raw compute, becomes the selling point for European AI buyers.
